_comment: An isolated molecular ion: CHO4S2(-1), 383 frames from OMol25.
Non-periodic, so there is no cell, no mesh and no slab correction --
and the long-range term is summed directly rather than in reciprocal
space. The frames carry a net charge AND a varying spin multiplicity,
which is what charge_spin.npy is for.
add_chg_spin_ebd is what makes the model READ charge_spin.npy at all.
It is part of DPA4C's structural signature, so in a multi-head model
it must be true for EVERY branch or the shared descriptor refuses to
link -- and turning it on later invalidates existing checkpoints.
default_chg_spin supplies the neutral-singlet fallback, so frames or
systems without a charge_spin.npy still run. It is deliberately NOT
part of the signature.
Charges are projected to the frame's total charge, taken from
column 0 of charge_spin -- so here they sum to -1, not 0.
method 'isolated' sums q_i q_j erf(alpha r)/r directly over every
pair. That is the SAME quantity the periodic branches evaluate in
reciprocal space -- their result converges onto it as the cell
grows -- so alpha must match whatever the periodic examples use.
No mesh, no spline order, no pbc, no slab_correction: all of those
describe a sum over periodic images, and passing one is an error
rather than a silent no-op.
No cutoff either -- erf(alpha r)/r decays as 1/r, so truncating it
would be wrong. Every pair is summed, which is O(N^2) and fine for
molecules (8 MiB at 1000 atoms).

loss._comment: start/limit_pref_v are 0: there is no cell, so no virial label.
